## Simple explanation

Explainable AI, or XAI, covers ways to help people understand what an AI
system is doing, why it produced an output, and where its limitations lie.
The same topic is also listed as [Explainable AI (XAI)](../E/explainable-ai-xai.qmd)
under E.

## Technical explanation

XAI includes intrinsically interpretable models, post-hoc explanations,
feature attribution, example-based explanations, counterfactuals, and
visualization. Methods may explain an individual prediction or summarize
behavior across a dataset. Explanations are approximations or representations
of model behavior and can be unstable, misleading, or mismatched to a user's
question.

## Why it matters in AI engineering

Explanations can support debugging, audits, human oversight, and
communication. They should be selected for a defined audience and decision;
an attractive explanation is not proof of fairness, causality, or correctness.

## How it works

First define what needs to be understood and by whom. Then select an approach
appropriate to the model and use case, test its fidelity and stability, and
evaluate whether intended users interpret it correctly. Monitor explanation
behavior when models or data change.

## Practical example

For a loan-risk model, a local explanation can show which input features
contributed to a score. Validate that the explanation reflects the model's
behavior, does not expose inappropriate information, and is understandable to
the people expected to use it.

## Common misconceptions

- Feature importance does not establish that a feature caused the prediction
  or outcome.
- A post-hoc explanation can be plausible while failing to faithfully
  represent the model.
